title: Runtime debugging: signal handoff and compact investigation dashboard design
content:
Purpose

This note captures a compact, investigation-first dashboard and a lightweight signal-handoff protocol aimed at reducing mean time to resolution (MTTR) for inference-runtime incidents. It focuses on what a responder needs within the first 3–5 minutes and how upstream teams should package signals when escalating.

Goals
- Reduce noisy alert triage by ensuring each alert includes a short, reproducible context bundle.
- Provide a single-screen investigative dashboard for on-call that answers: Is this customer impact, which stack layer, and is there a recent config or rollout change?
- Define metric and trace semantics so that cross-service correlation is reliable without overwhelming cardinality.

Design principles
- Investigation-first: surface causally useful signals (request path, model key, bucketed latency, recent rollout id).
- Low-cardinality primary keys: prefer 4–6 tagging dimensions on primary dashboards. High-cardinality attributes live in drilldowns only.
- Signal bundling: alarms include a one-line summary + 1-click bundle generation (S3 link or internal blob id) with the core fields below.

Core bundle fields (what should be attached to alerts/SLAs)
- alert_id: internal alert id
- example_request_id: a single request id that hit the issue window (trace id)
- time_window: start/end (UTC) for the anomaly
- primary_metrics_snapshot: snapshot of the 1–3 primary metrics (see metric definitions) with aggregation & percentile values
- top_spans: top 5 spans by duration from the example trace (span name, duration_ms, service)
- recent_rollout_tag: if a rollout was active, the rollout id and percentage
- affected_models: list of model ids hashed (not full model names to reduce leak risk)

Primary metrics (compact definitions for dashboard header)
1) user_request_rate_per_minute
- Type: count per minute aggregated by 1m windows
- Definition: number of accepted API requests (status in [200,202,206]) entering inference gateway
- Labels: region, deployment_tier (hosted/dedicated/private), model_bucket (see bucket guidance)
- Cardinality guidance: keep region x tier x model_bucket (<= 64 combos typically)
- What to show: current rate, 15m delta, and 95th percentile of request size

2) tail_token_latency_ms
- Type: distribution metric (histogram)
- Definition: end-to-end token emission latency (from request arrival to 1st token emitted and also per-token median) measured at front proxy
- Labels: region, model_bucket, route_type (sync/stream)
- Buckets: [0,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000,5000]
- What to show: P50/P95/P99 and heatmap for per-token slices

3) inference_error_rate_pct
- Type: ratio (errors / total requests * 100)
- Definition: requests ending in internal_error, model_timeout, or fallback_triggered. Exclude client validation errors.
- Labels: error_class (internal, model, infra), region, model_bucket
- Behavioral note: annotate spikes with fallback policy active flag

4) kv_cache_hit_rate
- Type: ratio (hits / lookups)
- Definition: backend KV cache hit rate for prefix-cache lookups for streaming contexts
- Labels: model_bucket, tenant_tier
- When low: correlate with increased token latency and cost per token

Cardinality and labeling guidance
- model_bucket: group models by architecture+size bucket (e.g., llama2-13b, opt-1.3b, quant-4bit). Use <= 12 buckets for dashboards.
- tenant_tier: host_free | host_paid | dedicated | private
- Avoid tenant_id or full model name in header widgets. Use hashed_model_id for drilldowns only.

Tracing/Span conventions for reliable handoff
- Trace id: use W3C traceparent propagated across proxy -> router -> runtime -> model-host. Log trace ids at entry+exit points.
- Example span names: proxy.receive, router.route, runtime.exec.prepare, runtime.exec.infer, model_host.decode, storage.kv.lookup
- Each span must include: span_id, parent_id, duration_ms, service, host_pool_id, rollout_id (if applicable), model_bucket, request_size_tokens
- Sampling: keep a low unbiased sample (1%) for long-term storage AND increased sampling (100%) for incidents flagged by alert rule for 5–15min windows.

On-call compact dashboard layout (single-screen)
Header (single-row):
- Alert banner (title + one-line cause hypothesis)
- 3 headline metrics: user_request_rate_per_minute, tail_token_latency_ms (P99), inference_error_rate_pct
- Quick links: open example trace, download bundle, related rollout

Main body (two columns)
Left column (big):
- Heatmap of per-token latency by model_bucket x region for the alert window (interactive)
- Top 5 slow traces (example request ids) with 1-click open to flamegraph

Right column (compact):
- Recent deploys / rollouts timeline (last 60m) with percentages and tags
- KV cache health (hit rate + 5m delta)
- Top error classes and counts
- Small table: top 10 tenants by error rate (hashed ids) with link to tenant usage page (drilldown only)

Drilldowns (secondary tabs)
- Full-span flamegraphs per example trace
- Latency histogram faceted by sequence length and prompt size
- Model-host metrics: GPU utilization, queue length, batch sizes

Operational playbook snippets
- If tail_token_latency_ms P99 > threshold AND kv_cache_hit_rate < 40%: suspect cache eviction pressure -> check recent model changes and cache config rollback button
- If inference_error_rate_pct spike AND recent_rollout_tag present: pause rollout to <1% and re-evaluate model variant
- If request_rate drops sharply and error rate rises: look at upstream auth / gateway throttling (check proxy.receive error class)

Signal handoff checklist for engineers escalating to SRE or model on-call
1) One-line summary with time window and user-visible impact
2) Attach example_request_id and generated bundle link
3) List of recent related PRs or rollouts (ids)
4) Quick hypothesis (short): model, infra, config, or traffic shift
5) Any temporary mitigations tried (rollback, scale-up, cache clear), and result

Open questions / next steps
- Automate bundle generation in alert runbook (prototype in ENG-7894).
- Define acceptable sampling ratio increase for traces during incidents to balance cost/privacy.
- Build a small internal Lambda to compute model_bucket mapping from registry for dashboard sync.

Appendix: short examples
- Example alert summary: "P99 token latency spike (route chat-stream) in us-west; error rate up 4.2% (11:03-11:08 UTC). example_request_id=trace-12a3b; recent_rollout=rollout-2025-11-03-13"
- Example quick triage: open trace -> see runtime.exec.infer spans dominant on model_host -> check model_host GPU queue and recent rollout -> if queue length > threshold, scale pool or fallback to older model variant.

Contact
- for implementation questions: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai), Marco Reyes (mreyes@redwood.ai)

Notes
- This doc intentionally prioritizes investigation ergonomics over metric exhaustiveness. Full metric catalog entries live in telemetry/catalog but those are heavy and not meant for the single-screen responder flow.
